# ERP UI language and design

- Write all user-facing ERP interface copy in natural Japanese. Do not add Chinese UI text.
- Keep the existing Japanese copy consistent; translate new labels, validation messages, empty states, dialogs, accessibility labels, and notifications into Japanese.
- Keep UI design simple, clean, and task-focused. Preserve the established visual system and interactions; prioritize clear hierarchy, readable spacing, responsive layouts, and accessibility.
- Avoid decorative clutter, unnecessary motion, visual effects, and controls that do not support a user task.
- Keep developer-facing identifiers and technical terms in English where appropriate; this policy applies to user-facing UI, not source identifiers.
- For UI changes, update the built asset with the repository build command and run the relevant UI tests and typecheck.
